objective: Implement v0.3.5 migration recovery so legacy <=0.3.3 users have a safe supported bootstrap path (refresh global launcher first, then update managed payload), launcher/payload divergence guidance is direction-aware, and a newer launcher can converge an older managed payload without downgrade or source checkout.
context: Issue #55 follows the BLOCKED v0.3.4 post-release acceptance in #54. Public v0.3.4 fresh install/lifecycle and provenance passed, but public v0.3.3 `dsh-crew update` cannot discover newer registry candidates because that immutable launcher predates registry-aware update. After refreshing only the launcher to 0.3.4, current status guidance incorrectly recommends downgrading the launcher back to the older payload. Do not claim immutable 0.3.3 itself is fixed. Define the supported migration boundary explicitly. Prefer a robust convergence rule: when the currently running global launcher is newer than the installed managed payload, `dsh-crew update` should be able to use the already-running validated package payload to converge the managed payload to that launcher version before considering a registry candidate, so `npm install -g @ran-sh/dsh-crew@latest` followed by `dsh-crew update` works even during registry propagation or pre-release candidate testing. When launcher and payload are equal, registry-aware update may discover a newer payload; when payload is newer than launcher, never downgrade payload and guide launcher refresh. Preserve Crew-owned Harness architecture and Harness-owned provider/model configuration.

validation: Validate the Task Contract and record the exact resolved source SHA.
Bump package.json, src/runtime-identity.mjs, and CHANGELOG.md to 0.3.5; keep exactly one bin dsh-crew -> ./bin/dsh-crew.mjs.

Implement and test direction-aware divergence semantics: launcher > payload instructs/runs managed-payload update and never suggests launcher downgrade; payload > launcher keeps payload and instructs launcher refresh; equal versions emit no divergence warning.

Implement a safe convergence path where a newer running launcher can serve as the validated update candidate for an older managed payload before registry resolution, while preserving stage/validate-before-switch, previous-release retention, config preservation, registration repair, and no-downgrade behavior.

Keep registry-aware update for equal-version/current installations so future public latest can still be discovered; candidate/registry failure remains fail-closed and must not damage the current payload or integrations.
Add regression coverage documenting immutable public 0.3.3 behavior as a legacy limitation rather than claiming its old update command can be changed retroactively.

In that migration flow plant config.json and .env sentinels and prove byte-identical preservation. Verify the prior usable release remains until successful activation and release retention stays bounded.
Exercise a failure case for candidate/registry resolution or validation and prove fail-closed behavior leaves the old payload and integrations usable.
Exercise same-version update/idempotence and fresh 0.3.5 global install -> install -> status -> update -> status -> uninstall -> status in a separate disposable home/prefix.
Verify source-checkout scripts/setup.mjs install -> status -> uninstall compatibility in a disposable home.

acceptance_criteria: Result status PASS with no blockers and explicit V035_MIGRATION_RECOVERY=PASS evidence.
A disposable real Windows migration from public launcher/payload 0.3.3 to local launcher/payload 0.3.5 succeeds via launcher refresh then dsh-crew update, with no source checkout requirement.

Launcher-newer/payload-older status/update behavior never recommends downgrading the launcher and converges the payload safely; payload-newer/launcher-older behavior never downgrades payload and gives correct launcher-refresh guidance.
Legacy <=0.3.3 migration boundary is documented accurately: old launcher update cannot be retroactively fixed; supported bootstrap is refresh launcher first, then update/install payload.
Config.json/.env remain byte-identical across migration/repair, failures are fail-closed, update remains no-downgrade/idempotent, and release retention is bounded.
Focused tests, full deterministic suite, build, both npm install verifiers, pack audit, publish dry-run, fresh global lifecycle, and source-checkout compatibility all PASS.
No real publication, dist-tag/tag/Release mutation, credential access, policy weakening, or official DSH mutation occurs.
